items.title: Claude Managed Agents session event streams now support event deltas
items.summary: Claude Managed Agents session event streams now support event deltas. Opt in with the event_deltas[] query parameter on GET /v1/sessions/{session_id}/events/stream. The event_start and event_delta…

explanation.what_it_is: Claude Managed Agents session event streams can now provide event deltas, which are the changes between events, rather than the full event data. This is enabled by adding the event_deltas query parameter to the GET /v1/sessions/{session_id}/events/stream API call.
explanation.why_it_matters: This change allows for more efficient processing of event streams, as only the changes between events need to be transmitted and processed. This can reduce the amount of data that needs to be handled, making it easier to work with large event streams.
how_to_use: Add the event_deltas query parameter to the GET /v1/sessions/{session_id}/events/stream API call to opt in to event deltas.
Use the event_start and event_delta fields in the response to process the event deltas.

items.title: Listing sessions for Claude Managed Agents now supports backward pagination
items.summary: Listing sessions for Claude Managed Agents now supports backward pagination. GET /v1/sessions returns a prev_page cursor alongside next_page; pass it as the page parameter to return to the previous…

explanation.what_it_is: The ability to list sessions for Claude Managed Agents now includes backward pagination, allowing you to retrieve previous pages of results.
explanation.why_it_matters: This update enables Claude Code users to more easily navigate and retrieve large lists of sessions, without having to start from the beginning every time.
how_to_use: Use the prev_page cursor returned by GET /v1/sessions to fetch the previous page of results by passing it as the page parameter.

Use the 'agent_with_overrides' type to customize the system prompt for a session

items.title: We've removed fast mode for Claude Opus 4.6
items.summary: We've removed fast mode for Claude Opus 4.6. Requests to claude-opus-4-6 with speed: "fast" no longer run at fast speed or premium pricing: they run at standard speed, are billed at standard rates,…

explanation.what_it_is: The 'fast mode' option has been removed for Claude Opus 4.6, meaning requests to this model will now run at standard speed regardless of the speed parameter set.
explanation.why_it_matters: This change affects billing, as requests that previously would have been billed at premium rates for fast mode will now be billed at standard rates, potentially altering cost estimates for Claude Code users.
how_to_use: Update your code to remove 'speed: fast' parameters for Claude Opus 4.6 requests, as they will have no effect.
Review your billing expectations, as the removal of fast mode and its associated premium pricing may reduce costs.

items.title: We've raised rate limits across the Claude API
items.summary: We've raised rate limits across the Claude API. Claude Sonnet and Claude Haiku rate limits now match Claude Opus at every usage tier, and usage tiers have been consolidated into three: Start, Build,…

explanation.what_it_is: The Claude API has increased its rate limits, allowing for more requests across all usage tiers. This change applies to all Claude models, including Claude Sonnet, Claude Haiku, and Claude Opus.
explanation.why_it_matters: This update enables Claude Code users to make more API requests without hitting rate limits, reducing the need for workarounds or tier upgrades. It simplifies the usage tiers into three categories: Start, Build, and another unnamed tier.
how_to_use: Check the updated rate limits for your usage tier to determine how many more requests you can make
Review your existing API integrations to identify opportunities to take advantage of the increased rate limits
Plan for potential increases in API usage without worrying about hitting previous rate limits

items.summary: We've launched Claude Fable 5 (claude-fable-5), our most capable widely released model, alongside Claude Mythos 5 (claude-mythos-5) for Project Glasswing participants. Both models support a 1M token…

explanation.what_it_is: Claude Fable 5 is a widely released model that supports up to 1M tokens, offering increased capability for Claude Code users. It is launched alongside Claude Mythos 5, which is available for Project Glasswing participants.
explanation.why_it_matters: This update matters because it provides Claude Code users with access to a more capable model, allowing them to process and generate larger amounts of text. This can be particularly useful for tasks that require longer input or output sequences.

Take advantage of the increased token limit to fine-tune the model on larger datasets, potentially leading to improved performance on specific tasks.

items.title: Claude Fable 5 and Claude Mythos 5 use the tokenizer introduced with Claude…
items.summary: Claude Fable 5 and Claude Mythos 5 use the tokenizer introduced with Claude Opus 4.7. Compared to models before Claude Opus 4.7, the same text produces roughly 30% more tokens. Use the token counting…

explanation.what_it_is: The tokenizer from Claude Opus 4.7 is now used in Claude Fable 5 and Claude Mythos 5, which increases the number of tokens produced for the same text by about 30%.
explanation.why_it_matters: This change affects how you count tokens for these models, as the same input text will now consume more tokens than it did with previous models.
how_to_use: Use the token counting tool to get an accurate count of tokens for your input text with Claude Fable 5 and Claude Mythos 5.
Adjust your token budgets accordingly to account for the increased token count.

items.title: Claude Fable 5 runs safety classifiers on requests and during response…
items.summary: Claude Fable 5 runs safety classifiers on requests and during response generation. When a classifier declines a request, the Messages API returns stop_reason: "refusal". You are not billed for a…

explanation.what_it_is: Claude Fable 5 now runs safety classifiers on both incoming requests and during the generation of responses, allowing for more controlled and safe interactions.
explanation.why_it_matters: This update changes how developers interact with the API, as requests that are deemed unsafe will be declined and return a 'refusal' stop reason, and users won't be billed for such declined requests.
how_to_use: Check the Messages API response for 'stop_reason: refusal' to handle declined requests
Use this feature to ensure compliance with safety guidelines in your application

items.title: On Claude Fable 5 and Claude Mythos 5, adaptive thinking is the only thinking…
items.summary: On Claude Fable 5 and Claude Mythos 5, adaptive thinking is the only thinking mode: thinking: {"type": "disabled"} is not supported, and manual extended thinking budgets and assistant prefill are not…

explanation.what_it_is: On Claude Fable 5 and Claude Mythos 5, adaptive thinking is now the sole thinking mode, with manual thinking mode and extended thinking budgets no longer supported.
explanation.why_it_matters: This change means Claude Code users can no longer disable thinking or manually set thinking budgets on these models, and must rely on adaptive thinking for all interactions.
how_to_use: Use adaptive thinking as the default thinking mode for all interactions with Claude Fable 5 and Claude Mythos 5
Remove any existing code that sets manual thinking modes or extended thinking budgets for these models

items.title: On Claude Fable 5 and Claude Mythos 5, thinking.display defaults to "omitted",…
items.summary: On Claude Fable 5 and Claude Mythos 5, thinking.display defaults to "omitted", the same as Claude Opus 4.8, Claude Opus 4.7, and Claude Mythos Preview; set display: "summarized" to receive readable…

explanation.what_it_is: The thinking.display default setting is now 'omitted' on Claude Fable 5 and Claude Mythos 5, meaning that thinking steps are not displayed by default.
explanation.why_it_matters: This change affects how models like Claude Fable 5 and Claude Mythos 5 return responses, requiring users to explicitly set display: 'summarized' to receive readable thinking steps.
how_to_use: Set display: 'summarized' in your API requests to receive readable thinking steps.
Update your existing code to handle the new default 'omitted' behavior.

Update your data retention settings if necessary to continue using Claude Fable 5
